To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we report the first molecularly confirmed case of intracannial EHE with a long clinical course of 16 years and a favorable outcome.
we report a case of meningeal epithelioid hemangiendothelioma (M-EHE) that was surgically treated 15 years after the initial detection of the tumor.
we describe an intracranial meningeal EHF with long-term favorable course and molecularly proven WWTR1-CAPTA1 gene fusion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the first case of meningeal EHF with WWTR1-CamTA1 gene rearrangement and slow growth.
a case of intracerebral EHE with a long-term favorable course.
the clinical course of intracranical EHE with WWTR1-CMATA1 gene rearrangement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the prognosis of meningeal EHA may not be as unfavorable as previously assumed.
EHE is a rare vascular tumor of the meninges with slow growth and favorable clinical course.
EHE is a slow growing tumor with an unpredictable clinical course, which may be associated with distant metastasis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the WWTR1-CMATA1 fusion is a driver for intracranially occurring EHE.
the WWTR1-CATMA1 fusion is a marker of EHE and not of a rapidly aggressive neoplasm.
EHE can present with a long-term indolent course, even in the intracranial compartment, and can be diagnosed based on histological, immunohistochemical, and genetic criteria.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the WWTR1-CAPMA1 fusion is a marker of intracranical EHE, even in slowly progressive tumors.
intracranial WWTR1-CMATA1 EHE may have an indolent clinical course and that the molecular signature may help in predicting the clinical course.
the clinical behavior of EHE is not predictable based on histology or molecular findings.
